clue.text: Drug bar at wild party for Indians

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
a latch is a bar that fastens a door or gate

explanation.surface: Someone is smuggling drugs into a raucous party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indians are Native Americans of the Pacific Northwest, not people from India.
explanation.definitionFit: A potlatch is a ceremonial feast of Northwest Coast Native American peoples, and informally any lavish, boisterous gathering.

clue.text: Clubman's quick rhymes

blocks.note: first meaning: the founder of the club in Dickens's first novel
second meaning: a pair of syllables, each a rhyme for quick

explanation.surface: A club member is reeling off some speedy verses.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Mr Pickwick founds the Pickwick Club in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers; both halves of his name, PICK and WICK, rhyme with 'quick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pickwick is the best-known fictional clubman, president of the club named after him in Dickens's first novel.

clue.text: Depends on follower for runs

blocks.note: something that depends on a factor turns on it; the 'on' is understood
a tail is someone who follows a suspect

explanation.surface: Someone relies on a sidekick to score runs, as in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depends on' stands for 'turns (on)', with 'on' doing double duty as the positional word placing the follower after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom for fleeing, which is one sense of running away.

clue.text: Quick article, as it happens

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a live broadcast goes out as events happen

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece written quickly, reporting events in real time.
explanation.walkthrough: Quick has an old sense of living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic sense of quick, preserved in the Creed's phrase about judging the living and dead, means having life.

clue.text: Stars horseman, so to speak

blocks.note: first meaning: the southern constellation Centaurus, known in English by this name
second meaning: a mythical creature that is literally part man and part horse

explanation.surface: A celebrity rider is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So to speak' flags that horseman is meant literally, a horse-man rather than a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation Centaurus is pictured as the mythical half-human, half-equine creature of Greek legend, which is a literal horse-man.

clue.text: Rarely producing new models

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A designer or factory that hardly ever brings out the latest versions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning not often, on few occasions, infrequently.

clue.text: One who improves parts of Notre Dame

indicators.note: breaking the name into parts and reassembling them reorders its letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A restorer working on sections of the Paris cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: An emendator corrects or amends texts, making changes that put them right.

clue.text: Circular objects in place of entertainment

blocks.note: a disc is a flat round object
the letter O is round too; the phrase serves for both pieces

explanation.surface: Round things standing in for some sort of show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular objects' is plural because it supplies two round things in a row, a disc and the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a nightclub where people dance to recorded music, a venue for amusement.

clue.text: Disorder for a month on the border

blocks.note: the fifth month
the hem is the turned-up border of cloth

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out on a frontier for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means sitting above, so the month comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent confusion or chaos, a state of serious unrest.

clue.text: Editor's put in news that's upset this country

indicators.note: something put in sits inside another word
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor's interference in a story has upset a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweden is a Scandinavian nation; the clue points at it as the country in question.

clue.text: Right filling for tooth, one sort of canine

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so one word is placed within another

blocks.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
R is the abbreviation for right
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dentist puts the correct filling into one canine tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Canine looks like a tooth, which suits 'filling', but here it is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: State of some Americans just off the Needles?

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the fifty US states, home to some Americans
second meaning: read as two words, a sweater only just finished on the knitting needles

explanation.surface: Some Americans live in a state lying just offshore from the Needles rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, and Jersey is a Channel Island not far away, so geography seems the path; a jersey is a knitted sweater, and the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state is named after the Channel Island, and its name also describes a freshly knitted sweater.

clue.text: Desolate region explored by Eliot

blocks.note: first meaning: barren, empty ground
second meaning: the title of T. S. Eliot's 1922 poem

explanation.surface: A bleak landscape that an explorer named Eliot investigated.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren uncultivated ground is called by this phrase, and The Waste Land is T. S. Eliot's famous modernist poem.

clue.text: Crowd in Channel port moving right to left

indicators.note: the letter for right is shifted leftwards and slotted in earlier in the word

blocks.note: Dover is the English port on the Channel

explanation.surface: A mass of people jostling in a ferry port.
explanation.walkthrough: The R at the end of DOVER moves forward to become the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd of animals being driven, and by extension a large moving throng of people.

clue.text: Room for audience for this sort of music

blocks.note: first meaning: a formal room where a ruler receives visitors
second meaning: music for a small ensemble, originally played in a private room

explanation.surface: A concert hall suited to listeners of a particular musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audience' means a formal interview with a monarch, not a crowd of listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a reception room in a palace, and chamber music is classical music for a few players.

clue.text: Cast off here for second part of journey

blocks.note: first meaning: where the actors wait when they are not on stage
second meaning: read as two words, the return leg of a trip

explanation.surface: A boat casts off at this point for the next leg of a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' looks nautical, but cast means actors, and 'off' means not performing.
explanation.definitionFit: The area behind a theatre's stage is where performers not in a scene wait; split up, the word is the leg of a trip home.

clue.text: Inform of tiny adjustment

indicators.note: an adjustment alters an arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Telling someone about a minor change.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify someone is to tell them formally, to give them the news.

clue.text: Allowed, say, the part below the crust of this port

indicators.note: say asks for the word spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: free to do something is allowed to do it
the mantle is the layer of the Earth beneath the crust

explanation.surface: A pie seems in view: the bit under the pastry crust is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Fremantle is the port city near Perth in Western Australia; its first syllable is pronounced like 'free'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fremantle is the main harbour of Western Australia, at the mouth of the Swan River.

clue.text: Chaps keep score in mind

blocks.note: chaps are men
a tally is a running score

explanation.surface: Some men keep count of the points in their heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentally means in the head, by thought alone, without writing anything down.

clue.text: Old saw that's lost its cutting edge

blocks.note: first meaning: a saw is a proverb or saying, and an old one is worn and trite
second meaning: a phrase that has gone blunt through overuse and no longer has any bite

explanation.surface: A blunt old woodworking tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a carpenter's tool, which 'cutting edge' supports, but it means a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed expression is an old saying worn so smooth by use that it has lost any force.

clue.text: Opposition makes two points in my case it appears

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the following word sits inside my

blocks.note: east and north, two points of the compass
taken as written
taken as written
surface padding that rounds off the sentence

explanation.surface: Someone argues that hostility arises, at least in their own situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In my case' reads as the idiom 'as for me', but here it means literally holding something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility, the state of being actively opposed to someone.

clue.text: Diet rich enough for so-called film star?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sufficiently nourishing diet

blocks.clueFragment: Diet rich enough for so-called film star
blocks.note: setter's reading: said aloud, the first two words are the surname of a screen legend, enough on their own to name her

explanation.surface: A film star is offered a diet that is nourishing enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet rich' sounds like Dietrich, so the surname alone is enough to pin down the star; the answer is her first name, Marlene Dietrich.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was the German-born Hollywood actress famous for The Blue Angel; her first name completes the identification.

clue.text: Kind of valve in heart gets second wind

indicators.note: the valve gets, that is takes into itself, the extra letter

blocks.note: the mitral valve is in the heart
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A heart patient's valve trouble leaves them short of breath again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second wind' reads as a recovery of breath; second gives only its letter and wind is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold north wind blowing down the Rhône valley in southern France.

clue.text: Airman in a kite can be counted on

blocks.note: kite and bus are both old slang for an aeroplane
AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank

explanation.surface: A reliable pilot is up in a light aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be counted on' looks like praise for the airman, but it describes a counting frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for doing arithmetic, so people literally reckon sums on it.

clue.text: Blackbirds in woods, for example

blocks.note: the one printed word is read as two, black and birds, each supplying a piece
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
owls are birds

explanation.surface: Blackbirds perched among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Blackbirds' splits into its two halves. Woods are the weighted balls used in the lawn game of bowls, so 'woods' is not trees.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game played on a green, the balls rolled are called woods, and each one is a bowl.

clue.text: Said to apply in this part of South-East

indicators.note: said asks for a word spoken, matching another in sound

blocks.note: to wield power or a tool is to apply it

explanation.surface: Something reportedly relevant to a region of south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is a formerly wooded area of Kent, Sussex and Surrey in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weald is the region between the North and South Downs in south-east England.

clue.text: Villainous crimes upset social worker

indicators.note: something upset is knocked into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of crimes rearranged
the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A social worker distressed by wicked offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer, but it is an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, miscreant describes someone wicked or depraved, behaving like a criminal.

clue.text: Strive to fix immovably inside

indicators.note: the letters sit within the phrase that precedes this word

blocks.note: found within these words

explanation.surface: An instruction to try hard to make something fast from within.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten with metal pins, so firmly that it cannot move, as an eye rivets on a sight.

clue.text: Letter or card

blocks.note: first meaning: a written symbol, such as a letter of the alphabet
second meaning: an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.walkthrough: Letter and card look like two kinds of post; a card is also a witty, odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed symbol is called this, and so is a colourful, eccentric individual whom one might also call a card.

clue.text: Essential for a showgirl with no capital left

indicators.note: the capital is the first letter, which is to be dropped

blocks.note: Evita is the title character of the Lloyd Webber musical
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Something indispensable for a chorus girl who has run out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money, but it is the head letter of the show's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means absolutely necessary, indispensable to something's survival or success.

clue.text: More down South, summer's not so sunny

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
a summer is someone who sums, an adder

explanation.surface: The weather in the south is gloomier: summer is less bright there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but one who adds up figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more down means more dejected, and not so sunny means less cheerful, both comparatives of unhappy.

clue.text: Butter more evenly spread to fry at the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: spread more evenly is flatter
the final letter of fry

explanation.surface: Kitchen advice: spread the butter more evenly to fry it properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter here is the noun for smooth talk, as in 'butter up'; 'to' is surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive praise, often called soft soap or butter, laid on to win favour.
